ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the region $0 \le x \le d$, there is a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the paper. In the region $x < 0$, there is a uniform electric field along the positive $y$-axis (not shown in the figure). A proton moves from point $P$ $(-\sqrt{3}d, -\frac{d}{2})$ with a velocity $v_0$ along the positive $x$-axis. At $t=0$, it enters the uniform magnetic field precisely at the origin $O$. The magnetic field varies according to the pattern shown in Figure (b), with the direction perpendicular to the plane of the paper and outward taken as positive. The mass of the proton is $m$, its charge is $e$, and gravity is negligible.

1. What is the magnitude and direction of the proton's velocity as it just enters the magnetic field?
2. If the proton exits the magnetic field along the $y$-axis within the time interval $0:\frac{T}{2}$, what is the minimum value of the magnetic induction $B$?
3. If the proton exits the magnetic field at point $M\ (d,\ 0)$ with the same velocity direction as when it entered the magnetic field, what are the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B_{\theta}$ and the period $T$ of the magnetic field variation?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}v_{0}$, at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ above the positive $x$-axis.
$\frac{\sqrt{3}mv_{0}}{e d}$
$\frac{4{\sqrt{3}}n mv_{0}}{3e d}$, $\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi d}{6nv_{0}}$ (n=1,2,3,\cdots)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached figure has two panels. In the left panel, the x-y axes are drawn with O at the origin. The magnetic-field region is the vertical strip from the y-axis x=0 to a dashed vertical line at x=d; the point M is on the x-axis at the right boundary. Black dots in the strip indicate magnetic field out of the page. A proton starts from point P to the left with horizontal velocity v0 toward +x, and the entry velocity at O is shown slanting upward to the right. In the right panel, the B-t graph is a square wave: B is positive from 0 to T/2, negative from T/2 to T, positive from T to 3T/2, and negative from 3T/2 to 2T; outward is defined as positive. Reasoning: In the region x<0, the electric field is vertical, so the horizontal velocity remains vx=v0. The proton moves horizontally from P to O through distance sqrt(3)d, so the flight time before reaching O is tau=sqrt(3)d/v0. Its vertical displacement is from -d/2 to 0, namely d/2, with initial vertical velocity zero. Under constant vertical acceleration, d/2=(vy(O)/2)tau, so vy(O)=d/tau=v0/sqrt(3). Therefore the speed on entering the magnetic field is V=sqrt(v0^2+(v0/sqrt(3))^2)=2sqrt(3)v0/3, and tan(alpha)=vy/vx=1/sqrt(3), so alpha=30 degrees above +x. For part 2, during 0 to T/2 the graph shows a constant positive, outward magnetic field. For a positive proton entering at 30 degrees above +x, the Lorentz force bends the path clockwise. Let R=mV/(eB). The circle center is one radius in the force direction from O, so C=(R/2,-sqrt(3)R/2). The largest x-coordinate on that circle is Cx+R=3R/2. To exit through the y-axis without crossing the boundary x=d, require 3R/2<=d. The minimum B corresponds to the maximum allowed R, R=2d/3. Hence B_min=mV/(eR)=m(2sqrt(3)v0/3)/(e*2d/3)=sqrt(3)mv0/(ed). For part 3, use one positive-B arc followed by one negative-B arc of the same radius R. The first half-interval bends the velocity clockwise, the next half-interval bends it back by the same angle, so the final direction can equal the original entry direction. To make the S-shaped cell return to y=0, the turn angle in each half-interval is 60 degrees, i.e. omega T/2=pi/3. One such cell advances horizontally by 2R. If n identical cells fill the width d, then 2nR=d, so R=d/(2n). With V=2sqrt(3)v0/3, B_theta=mV/(eR)=4sqrt(3)n mv0/(3ed). Also omega=eB_theta/m, and omega T/2=pi/3 gives T=sqrt(3)pi d/(6nv0), where n=1,2,3,... Final answer separated below.
